transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with some really intense thoughts and beliefs that other people tell me aren't actually real. It's gotten to the point where it's taking over my life, and I just really need some help.

Have there been times when you felt extremely high or energized, or very depressed, for days or longer around the same time as these beliefs? Or have these beliefs happened even when your mood felt normal?

Yes, I've definitely had times where I felt incredibly high and energized while experiencing these thoughts. But there have also been periods, lasting for at least two weeks or more, where my mood felt completely normal and stable, yet those beliefs were still happening.
During those high and energized times, did you also need much less sleep and feel more talkative, impulsive, or unusually confident than usual?

During those times, I definitely get extremely talkative, speaking so fast that people can't even interrupt me, and I feel this surge of intense confidence like I have special abilities. I'm not really sure about my sleep or being impulsive, but the constant talking and feeling of power were definitely there.
Over the whole time you’ve been ill, have these high-energy or depressed mood episodes been present for most of the illness, or have the unusual beliefs been there mainly without major mood symptoms?

Looking back at the two and a half years I've been dealing with this, those high-energy episodes have definitely been present for most of that time. However, there have still been those periods of at least two weeks where the unusual beliefs and hallucinations happened completely on their own without any high energy.
Have you also had major depressive episodes during this illness, with at least two weeks of feeling very down or losing interest most of the day nearly every day?

No, I haven't really had periods of feeling down or losing interest in things. My mood struggles have always been the opposite, where I feel extremely energetic, elevated, or sometimes really irritable.

This pattern argues against Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features, since psychosis is not confined to mood episodes, and against Schizophrenia, since prominent mood episodes have been present for the majority of the illness. The absence of major depressive episodes also supports the bipolar type rather than depressive type.
